senses.def: a hard green stone used for jewellery and decoration
ex: She wore a jade bracelet.
The statue is carved from jade.

senses.def: a place where people are kept as a punishment for a crime
ex: He spent two years in jail.
She was sent to jail for theft.

senses.def: a glass container with a wide top, used for food
ex: There's a jar of jam in the cupboard.
He filled the jar with coins.

senses.def: special words used by a particular group that other people find hard to understand
ex: The report is full of legal jargon.
Avoid technical jargon when you write.

senses.def: unpleasant and not fitting with what is around it
ex: The loud music was jarring in the quiet café.
The bright colours made a jarring contrast.

senses.def: the lower part of the face that moves when you speak or eat
ex: He hit the boxer on the jaw.
Her jaw dropped in surprise.

senses.def: a type of music with a strong rhythm, often played without written notes
ex: He plays the saxophone in a jazz band.
I love listening to jazz.

senses.def: unhappy because you want what someone else has
ex: She was jealous of her sister's success.
Don't be jealous.

senses.def: unhappy because you think someone you love likes another person
ex: He gets jealous when she talks to other men.

mistake.wrong: He is jealous on his friend.
mistake.right: He is jealous of his friend.

senses.def: to put something in danger of being lost or harmed
ex: Bad behaviour could jeopardize your job.
The delay jeopardized the whole project.

senses.def: a shirt worn by a sports player
ex: He wore a red football jersey.

senses.def: a warm knitted top (British English)
ex: Put on a jersey; it's cold.

senses.def: made of a soft stretchy cloth
ex: She bought a jersey dress.

senses.def: a valuable stone such as a diamond
ex: The crown was covered in jewels.
She kept her jewels in a safe.

senses.def: the work that you do regularly to earn money
ex: She has a new job in a bank.
He is looking for a job.

senses.def: a piece of work that you have to do
ex: Cleaning the car is a hard job.

mistake.wrong: I have a lot of jobs to do at work, so I'm tired from the job.
mistake.right: I have a lot of work to do.
mistake.note: 'Job' is a countable position, while 'work' is the uncountable activity.

senses.def: shared or done by two or more people together
ex: They opened a joint bank account.
It was a joint decision.

senses.def: a place where two bones meet in the body
ex: My knee joints hurt.
He has pain in his hip joint.

senses.def: a large piece of meat cooked in an oven
ex: We had a joint of beef for lunch.

senses.def: something you say or do to make people laugh
ex: He told us a funny joke.
It was only a joke.

senses.def: to say things that are not serious in order to be funny
ex: I'm only joking.
They joked about the weather.

senses.def: a serious magazine, usually about a special subject
ex: She published her research in a medical journal.

senses.def: a book where you write about what happens to you each day
ex: He wrote in his journal every night.

senses.def: the work of collecting and writing news for newspapers, television or websites
ex: She studied journalism at university.
He has a career in journalism.

senses.def: a person whose job is to collect and write news
ex: The journalist interviewed the mayor.
She works as a journalist for a newspaper.

senses.def: the act of travelling from one place to another
ex: It was a long journey by train.
Have a safe journey!

mistake.wrong: I enjoyed my journey in Spain for two weeks.
mistake.right: I enjoyed my two-week trip to Spain.
mistake.note: 'Journey' is the travel from one place to another, while 'trip' includes the visit itself.

senses.def: a feeling of great happiness
ex: She jumped for joy.
The baby brought joy to the family.

senses.def: an opinion or decision formed after thinking carefully
ex: I trust her judgment.
It's too soon to make a judgment.

senses.def: an official decision made by a judge
ex: The court gave its judgment on Friday.

senses.def: a sport from Japan in which two people try to throw each other to the ground
ex: He trains at a judo club twice a week.
She won a medal in judo.

senses.def: containing a lot of juice
ex: This is a juicy orange.
The meat was soft and juicy.

senses.def: a warm knitted piece of clothing for the upper body
ex: She wore a blue woollen jumper.
Take a jumper in case it gets cold.

senses.def: a thick tropical forest where many plants and animals live
ex: Tigers live in the jungle.
They walked through the thick jungle.

senses.def: having a lower position in an organisation
ex: She is a junior doctor.
He started as a junior clerk.

senses.def: for or relating to young people
ex: He plays in the junior team.

senses.def: the official power to make legal decisions in a particular area
ex: The case is outside this court's jurisdiction.
Each state has its own jurisdiction.

senses.def: a member of a jury
ex: Each juror listened carefully to the evidence.

senses.def: a group of ordinary people who decide in a court whether someone is guilty
ex: The jury found him not guilty.
She was called for jury duty.

senses.def: a group of people who judge a competition
ex: The jury chose the best film.

senses.def: a very short time ago
ex: I have just finished my homework.
She just left.

senses.def: only, or simply
ex: I just want some water.
It's just a small problem.

senses.def: exactly or very recently
ex: This is just what I needed.

mistake.note: Do not use the present perfect with a finished time such as 'yesterday'.

senses.def: fair treatment of people according to what is right
ex: Everyone wants justice.
She fought for social justice.

senses.def: the system of law and courts
ex: The accused was brought to justice.

senses.def: to show that something is reasonable or right
ex: How can you justify this price?
Nothing can justify violence.

senses.def: a young person who is not yet an adult (formal)
ex: The court deals with juveniles separately.

senses.def: relating to young people, or silly like a child
ex: Juvenile crime has fallen.
His jokes are rather juvenile.
